census_artifacts.statement: Shows that a finite ordinary marginal negative mark moment does not give the short-bar density exponent; the moment has to be taken under the limiting collision-mark measure with the D1 joint-law, envelope and selection hypotheses. Example: if r has density 3r^2 on (0,1), k=r and ell = k r^3 = r^4, then E[k^-1] = 3/2 is finite, yet the exact lifetime density is (3/4) ell^(-1/4), not ell^0. This is stated as consistent with D1, which keeps those hypotheses.

census_artifacts.statement: Correction to the claim that Conjecture Z is 'well posed': a log-CDF limit alone gives a cumulative scaling exponent, not a density theorem. Counterexample: a measure with atoms at 2^-n and masses 2^-n has log-CDF exponent 1 but no Lebesgue density. Also notes that for T-CUE at beta=1 a merely bounded nonlocal short-bar density can contribute at the same order as the proposed constant, so the four local D1 hypotheses alone do not identify the full bar coefficient. That second point is stated without proof.
